subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation — next steps and POC plan

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation — post-call recap

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to capture next steps: 

- Requirements you shared: sustained 120 QPS inference for 512-token average responses, 99.9% availability during business hours, and the ability to absorb weekly batch inference jobs that spike both throughput and memory usage.
- Main concern: vendor capacity guarantees during those batch windows — you mentioned previous outages with burst demand on hyperscaler on-demand capacity.
- Success criteria for the eval: match latency SLO (p95 < 120ms), demonstrate sustained throughput for 2 hours, and a cost comparison (monthly TCO) between Redwood Dedicated reserved pools and the hyperscaler reserved/spot mix.

Next steps we agreed on:
1) Redwood to share an initial POC/test plan (SE owner: Lauren).
2) Provide a short pricing deck for Dedicated + a cost model comparing to hyperscaler reserved instances (Commercial: me).
3) Run an initial 2-hour stress test and a cold-start/scale-up run.
4) Procurement contact for MAP/PO — Jordan to introduce (if needed).

I’m attaching the pricing deck and a sample test plan. Lauren will follow up with the technical checklist and required artifacts (model + sample dataset, expected QPS profile).

If anything above looks off, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise Lauren — could you drop the test plan and timing options?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Markus — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 120 QPS target is sustained for typical daytime traffic, but we get periodic batch jobs that can bump to ~400 QPS for 30–90 minutes. Our main worry is that hyperscaler on-demand pools throttled us during a previous campaign. Can Redwood guarantee capacity during those windows if we reserve Dedicated pools? What are your SLA/credits for capacity failures?
- For procurement: we generally run a 12–24 month commit for reserved capacity if the economics justify it. Can you include a 12-month vs 24-month pricing comparison?
- I’m attaching our security/QA packet with a few required items to pre-validate for the PoC.

Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation — test plan and artifacts

Hi Jordan —

Attached is the proposed PoC test plan (spreadsheet) and a short checklist of artifacts we’ll need from your side. High-level plan: 

1) Kickoff & environment setup (Day 0–1): exchange keys, provide sample model + dataset, configure Dedicated pool.
2) Baseline runs (Day 2): run existing workloads at current config for baseline metrics.
3) Sustained throughput test (Day 3): 2-hour sustained run at 120 QPS; measure p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates.
4) Burst window test (Day 4): simulate batch spike up to 400 QPS for 45 minutes; validate capacity without throttling.
5) Cold-start & autoscale test (Day 5): large-scale spike from idle to 120 QPS to measure scale-up time.
6) Cost & kernel-level profiling: we’ll run identical tests on a hyperscaler reserved instance configuration (we’ll model the infra/VM spec you provide) and return a cost/TCO comparison.

Things we need from you: sample model binary (or HF model id), representative request traces (anonymized), and a point of contact for procurement to receive draft contracts.

Proposed windows: week of Aug 10 or Aug 17. We can accommodate a two-week POC if you want extra validation.

I’ve attached acme-poc-test-plan.xlsx which includes the synthetic load parameters and the hyperscaler VM mapping for the cost model.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation — commercial and timing

Jordan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the QA packet. A few commercial notes to set expectations ahead of the PoC: 

- Capacity guarantees: Redwood Dedicated is architected as a reserved GPU pool with capacity isolation. For committed reserved contracts (12/24 months) we provide throughput SLOs and formal credits if we fail to meet availability/throughput targets during business hours; specifics will be in the T&Cs but I’ll include a short SLA summary in the next deck.
- Cost model: we’ll provide a 12- vs 24-month committed pricing comparison and a modeled hyperscaler equivalent (reserved instance pricing + networking). Our initial estimate shows Dedicated gives stronger tail-latency consistency and simpler capacity guarantees versus a mixed hyperscaler reserved/spot approach, but we’ll validate with the PoC.
- Tests & timing: Lauren’s suggested windows (week of Aug 10 or Aug 17) work for us. Suggest we kick off Aug 10 so results land before your procurement review.

I’ve linked the shared drive with the draft PoC plan and added this to our CRM: HS-98321. If procurement wants an NDA or template contract early, loop in Rachel and she’ll coordinate.

Proposed next steps:
- Jordan to share model + traces and procurement contact by EOD Fri (Jul 24).
- Redwood to deliver updated pricing deck with SLA summary by Mon (Jul 27).
- Kickoff call Aug 10.

Deal: ACME-2113

Thanks,
Markus
